mem.t: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.

lessons.title: Nine Fruits, One Life
lessons.theme: The nine fruits are not nine assignments but the one life of Christ

v: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,
gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.
I am the vine. You are the branches. He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.

lessons.still: Slowly read the nine fruits aloud: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Pause after each one, and recall one way the Lord has spoken to you about that fruit during this stage.
teach: This is the retreat week of Stage 3, “Fruiting: The 920 Practice.” Thirteen weeks ago we set out from “everyone is my 2,” then practised the nine fruits one by one, and finally learned about forgiveness and restoration and the rhythm of life. This week we stop, like a farmer looking back at harvest time, to count: what fruit has the Lord produced in me?

Notice that the word Paul uses for “fruit” is singular in the original. The nine fruits are not nine separate virtues from which we can pick a few to work on; they are nine aspects of one life — like a bunch of grapes with many grapes, all growing on the same branch. That life is Christ himself: “He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit.”

So the point of our review is not “How well have I done?” but “Have I been remaining in the Lord?” When there is little fruit, the reason is not too little effort but too little connection. “Apart from me you can do nothing” — this is not only a warning; it is also a promise: joined to the Lord, we will surely bear fruit.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Fruit is the life of Christ flowing naturally from those who live the self-emptied life; it is not produced by our own self-improvement. Self-ruled people try to “manufacture” fruit and end up exhausted and fake; people living the self-emptied life abide in the Lord, and the fruit grows naturally. Let Jesus receive all the glory — even our fruit is his.
q: Who is God? — The vine supplies everything the branches need — what does this show you about the Lord?
Who am I? — Of the nine fruits, which has grown most visibly in you during this stage? Which most needs to grow?
How shall I respond? — How will you “remain in the Lord” more deeply?
lessons.jesus: The nine fruits are fully displayed in Jesus: he loved to the end; he rejoiced in the Holy Spirit; he gave people peace; he was patient through it all; he was kind to sinners; he went about doing good; he is faithful and true; he is gentle and humble in heart; and he obeyed perfectly in temptation. He is the true vine.
lessons.pray: Lord, the true vine, thank you for working in me during this stage. I confess that apart from you I can do nothing; all fruit is your life. Help me to remain in you more deeply, and let the nine fruits flow out of my life more abundantly, all to your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down the nine fruits, and beside each one write an experience from this stage
Share with one of “my 2” one fruit the Lord has produced in you
lessons.noon: “He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit.” — Lord, right now I remain in you.

lessons.title: How My 2 Have Changed
lessons.theme: Love is seen in relationships, and that is where disciples are recognised

v: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also love one another.
By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.”

lessons.still: Take out the “my 2” list you wrote in Week 27 (if you don’t have one, list them in your mind). Pause quietly at each name, and reflect: what has changed between us during this stage?
teach: A mirror can’t show you the back of your head; sometimes we only see how we have really changed through other people’s eyes. The best report card for this stage’s practice is not in our own notebooks but in the lives of our 2: Does my family find me gentler? Do my colleagues find me more reliable?

Jesus said, “By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.” The mark of a disciple is not knowledge, not gifts, not how many meetings we attend, but love. And this love has a standard: “Just as I have loved you, you also love one another.” This love must be seen in real, specific people.

Be honest as you review: some relationships have improved, some are still hard, and some may even be more tense. Don’t be discouraged, and don’t boast. Relationships often change slowly, like the turning of the seasons. What matters is this: have I begun to see my 2 through Christ’s eyes? A changed life changes relationships.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The fivefold change — mindset, life, lifestyle, relationships, ministry. The practice of 920 is letting the change in our lives flow into our relationships. Every person in my life is my 2; when I live out the “0” of the self-emptied life, they will see the “9” of Christ in me.
q: Who is God? — Jesus says, “Just as I have loved you” — how has he loved you during this stage?
Who am I? — In the eyes of your 2, how have you changed during this stage?
How shall I respond? — Which of your 2 will you take special care to love in the next stage?
lessons.jesus: Jesus walked with his disciples for three years. His love was not from a distance; it was lived out eating together, walking together, being misunderstood together. On the last night, he washed his disciples’ feet, showing them by his actions what “just as I have loved you” means.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for loving me with your love, and for placing my 2 in my life. For the relationships that have changed, I give you the glory; the ones that are still hard, I place in your hands. Let everyone recognise by my love that I am your disciple. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Review your “my 2” list, and beside each name write one change
Ask a family member or close friend: “How do you think I have changed over this time?”
Write a thank-you card to one of “my 2,” thanking them for growing alongside you
lessons.noon: “By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.” — Lord, right now let people recognise you in me.

lessons.title: Testimonies of Grace in Relationships
lessons.theme: By the grace of God I am what I am

v: But we all, with unveiled face seeing the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, even as from the Lord, the Spirit.
But by the grace of God I am what I am. His grace which was given to me was not futile, but I worked more than all of them; yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.

lessons.still: Recall a moment of grace in one of your relationships during this stage: an act of forgiveness, a reconciliation, a gentle word, a patient evening. Don’t analyse it; simply give thanks, and let that grace warm your heart once more.
teach: The moon gives no light of its own; its light is reflected from the sun. When people see moonlight at night, they are really seeing the sun. Paul says, “We all, with unveiled face seeing the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory.” The changes in our relationships are a reflection of the Lord’s glory.

Paul looked back on the change in his own life: from persecutor of the church to apostle of the gospel. He said, “By the grace of God I am what I am.” He admitted that he “worked more than all of them,” but immediately added, “yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.” The point of a testimony is not what I have done but what grace has done.

Today, prepare a “testimony of grace in a relationship”: what the relationship was like before, how God stepped in, and what has changed now. Keep it simple and true, and give the glory to God. A testimony is not showing off spiritual achievements; it lets people see that the God who could change me can change you too. This is also the first step towards multiplying.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Let Jesus receive all the glory. A self-ruled testimony exalts our own effort; a self-emptied testimony exalts God’s grace. The last step on the path of service is “God” — giving glory to God and giving thanks in everything. A testimony offers the fruit of our relationships back to the Lord.
q: Who is God? — “Even as from the Lord, the Spirit” — who does this show you is the source of change?
Who am I? — In which relationship have you seen God’s grace most clearly?
How shall I respond? — How will you share this testimony so that the Lord is glorified?
lessons.jesus: After Jesus healed the man possessed by demons, he said to him, “Go to your house, to your friends, and tell them what great things the Lord has done for you, and how he had mercy on you.” Testimonies of grace begin in our closest relationships.
lessons.pray: Lord of grace, by your grace I am what I am. Thank you for working in my relationships and freeing me, little by little, from the bondage of the self-ruled life. Let my testimony never exalt myself, but help people see your work that goes from glory to glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write a three-part testimony: what it was like before, how God stepped in, and how it is now
Share this testimony of grace with one of “my 2”
Offer a prayer of thanksgiving for all of your 2
lessons.noon: “But by the grace of God I am what I am.” — Lord, right now all the glory is yours.

lessons.title: Stage Self-Review
lessons.theme: Honest review before God is for renewal, not condemnation

v: Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts.
See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.
being confident of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.

lessons.still: Quietly invite the Holy Spirit to shine into your heart like a gentle light. Say, “Search me, God.” Don’t rush to give yourself a score; first sit a while before the Lord, remembering that you are his beloved child, and only then begin your self-review.
teach: The purpose of a health check-up is not to frighten us but to catch problems early and treat them properly. The Stage 3 spiritual health self-review is the same: we are not handing God a report card; we are telling the Doctor honestly how we are, so that he can heal, adjust, and guide our next steps.

David prayed, “Search me, God, and know my heart… See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.” He did not search himself; he asked God to search him. As you review yourself, let the Holy Spirit lead you, not your own feelings. Paul also says, “He who began a good work in you will complete it.”

As you review, you might ask: Is my relationship with God closer than it was thirteen weeks ago? Of the nine fruits, which has grown most and which least? How have my relationships with my 2 changed? Am I more able to forgive, and does my life have more rhythm? Answer honestly, then hand the results to the God who will surely complete the good work he began.
lessons.light: 321 Light: These are the “Review” and “Correction” steps of the eight steps for changing our mindset. Self-review is not self-blame; it is reviewing in grace and correcting under the Holy Spirit’s guidance, so that we can keep practising and move towards multiplication. Keep your focus on Jesus; he will complete the work he began.
q: Who is God? — “Will complete it” — how do you trust this God who never gives up halfway?
Who am I? — During this stage, what growth are you most grateful for? And what do you most need?
How shall I respond? — Based on your self-review, what one thing will you adjust in the next stage?
lessons.jesus: By the Sea of Tiberias, Jesus asked Peter three times, “Do you love me?” It was not an interrogation; it was helping Peter face himself honestly, and then entrusting him again: “Feed my sheep.” The Lord’s searching always comes with a call to renewal.
lessons.pray: Search me, God, and know my heart; see if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way. I hand over to you both my growth and my shortcomings in this stage. Thank you for beginning a good work in me; you will surely complete it. Guide my next step. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Complete this stage's spiritual health self-review
Write down the growth you are most grateful for, and one area to adjust
Ask one of “my 2”: “In what area do you think I can still grow?”
lessons.noon: “Search me, God, and know my heart.” — Lord, right now I open myself before you.

lessons.title: Resolving to Multiply
lessons.theme: Bearing fruit is not the finish line; the fruit is meant to last

v: “In this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit; and so you will be my disciples.

You didn’t choose me, but I chose you and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain; that whatever you will ask of the Father in my name, he may give it to you.

lessons.still: Quietly consider: of the fruit the Lord has produced in me during this stage, which could become a seed in someone else’s life? Bring one person’s face to mind and ask, “Lord, use me to be a blessing in their life.”
teach: An apple holds several seeds; each one could grow into a tree, and each tree could bear many apples. The ultimate purpose of fruit is not to be admired but to multiply. This week we have reviewed the nine fruits (Day 1), how my 2 have changed (Day 2), testimonies of grace (Day 3), and the stage self-review (Day 4).

Jesus said, “In this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit.” And again, “I chose you and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain.” Fruit that “remains” does not wither after one season; it is life passing on life, generation after generation. This is the Lord’s own choosing and appointing, not our own ambition.

In the next stage, we move from Fruiting to Multiplying: from bearing fruit ourselves to helping others bear fruit too; from being accompanied to accompanying others. Life first, then relationships, then ministry — having Christ’s life and having borne fruit in our relationships, we can now multiply naturally. You don’t need to be perfect; you only need to be willing.
lessons.light: 321 Light: One purpose — to build what belongs to God. The nine fruits in one person are a testimony; in many people, they become a display of the kingdom. In the next stage, the 235 journey begins: 2 spiritual companions, 3 spiritual parents and children, 5 fellow soldiers. Let Jesus receive all the glory.
q: Who is God? — The Lord has “chosen” and “appointed” you to bear fruit — how does this change the way you see your life?
Who am I? — Do you think you are not yet good enough to help others?
How shall I respond? — What resolution will you make as you enter the next stage of multiplying?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.” He himself is that grain of wheat: he died and rose again, and bore countless grains — including you and me. The road to multiplication is the road of the self-emptied life.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for choosing me and appointing me to bear fruit. All the fruit of this stage is your grace. I resolve to enter the next stage, not only bearing fruit myself but also willing to become a seed in other people’s lives. Make my fruit remain, so that the Father is glorified. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write a one-sentence resolution: “In the next stage, I am willing to…”
Say to one of “my 2”: “I’d love to grow in the Lord together with you.”
Pray with your spiritual companion, entrusting the next stage to the Lord
lessons.noon: “In this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit.” — Lord, right now I want to bear fruit that remains.
